facility_roles.quote: The Extended Baryon Oscillation Spectroscopic Survey (eBOSS) will conduct novel cosmological observations using the BOSS spectrograph at Apache Point Observatory.

notes: external.inspire_experiment is left null: INSPIRE-HEP was not contacted (STREAM_RULES forbid it), so no INSPIRE experiment recid could be fetched.
eBOSS data are part of the SDSS Collaboration; no separate eBOSS collaboration record exists.

No predecessor lineage to BOSS is recorded: the fetched pages call eBOSS a survey of a later SDSS generation that reuses the BOSS spectrographs and combines with BOSS results, but none uses the word predecessor or successor.

physics_goals.quote: eBOSS will use four different tracers to measure the distance-redshift relation with baryon acoustic oscillations (BAO).
physics_goals.value: Measure the distance-redshift relation with baryon acoustic oscillations using four tracers: luminous red galaxies, emission-line galaxies, quasars and the Lyman-alpha forest.

summary.plain: The Extended Baryon Oscillation Spectroscopic Survey, part of SDSS-IV, mapped galaxies and quasars from when the universe was 3 to 8 billion years old, a critical time when dark energy started to affect its expansion, and measured how fast space was expanding then.
summary.technical: SDSS-IV survey with the BOSS spectrographs on the 2.5-m telescope at Apache Point, dark-time observations July 2014 to March 2019: luminous red galaxies (0.6<z<1.0), emission-line galaxies (0.6<z<1.1) and quasars (0.8<z<3.5) for BAO and RSD measurements at 1–2% precision between 0.6<z<2.5.
